Subject: Case study + logo use for product launch

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the support on the pilot — our product and your inference throughput were a huge part of the results we shared internally. Marketing would like to publish a short case study and a one-paragraph quote from our Head of ML, plus use the Acuvera logo on Redwood's site and a joint press blurb timed with our Q1 product announcement.

Attached is a quick request packet (Acuvera_CaseStudy_Request.pdf) that highlights the quote, a draft blurb, and the logo files. Two quick asks: 1) confirmation that Redwood is ok with a short customer quote and logo on the Redwood customer page; 2) whether you have any embargo or approval windows we need to follow.

We are comfortable with a review window of 3 business days for the quote and want to ensure any confidentiality carveouts are respected. Happy to route this through legal if needed.

Best,
Susan Li
Head of Marketing, Acuvera Labs
press@acuvera.com

Questions from my side:
- Are there any standing MSA/order-form publicity carveouts we should be aware of for this customer?

Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Case study + logo use for product launch

Thanks for the ping, Sean. I reviewed the attached request and our current MSA (customer-facing) includes a standard publicity clause that allows customer logos and short quotes with prior written consent. For Acuvera I recommend we: 

1) Keep a short consent clause on the Order Form: customer grants Redwood the right to publish the customer name, logo, and a single short quote (<= 2 sentences) referencing the engagement. Consent is revocable with 30 days notice.

2) Add a narrow confidentiality carveout: Redwood may not publish any benchmark figures, raw telemetry, or PII derived from the engagement. Any performance claims must be mutually agreed in writing.

3) Approval window: 3 business days for quote/asset approval is acceptable; if Acuvera wants a longer review, we can accept up to 5 business days but prefer 3 to keep the go-to-market timing.

4) Embargo and synchronization: include an optional embargo date clause where both parties coordinate the public announcement; neither party can publish until the agreed embargo date.

5) If marketing assets include a product screenshot or derived metric, require explicit written authorization and include a short carveout that allows Acuvera to redact proprietary product names.

I attached suggested redline edits (redline_MSA_orderform_Acuvera_20261126.docx). Key change excerpts to include inline when we send to Acuvera: 

--- excerpt ---
"Customer grants Redwood the non-exclusive right to use Customer's name, logo, and a short (<=2 sentence) testimonial in marketing materials and on Redwood's website, subject to Customer's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Redwood shall not publish any raw performance data or internal telemetry without Customer's express written consent."
--- end excerpt ---

If Acuvera insists on a blanket publicity prohibition, we should escalate for commercial trade-off (e.g., extended free credits or marketing assistance).

I'll mark up the Order Form with the above and we can route to Sean for final send to Acuvera.

- Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Susan — thanks for the packet. Looping in Kimberly with a suggested redline and Dev to coordinate the exact logo variants. Per Kimberly's guidance below, attached is our proposed Order Form redline that adds: (a) a scoped publicity consent (name, logo, <=2 sentence quote), (b) explicit prohibition on publishing raw benchmarks/telemetry without mutual sign-off, and (c) an optional embargo date field.

Please review the attached redline_MSA_orderform_Acuvera_20261126.docx. For speed, if you approve the language as-is we can include the clause in the Order Form and push the DocuSign envelope today (link included). If you'd like changes, let us know the specific edits; we'd ask for a 3-business-day approval window on the quote/asset by default.

Inline excerpt for quick reference: "Redwood shall not publish any raw performance data or internal telemetry without Customer's express written consent. Customer's approval on quoted text shall be provided within three (3) business days of submission, and shall not be unreasonably withheld."

Next steps:
- Susan to confirm approval or provide edits (3 business days).
- Dev to confirm logo sizes/variants (SVG + PNG).
- If approved, we will send updated Order Form via DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/1234abcd

Thanks — Sean

Sean / Kimberly / Dev — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. Acuvera is broadly comfortable with the proposed language. Two small requests: (1) can we extend the quote approval window to four (4) business days instead of three given our comms calendar?; (2) we need a 7-day embargo after our internal counsel signs off (i.e., internal sign-off + 7 days before joint announcement) to allow coordination with partners.

We accept the restriction on raw telemetry and agree that performance claims will be mutually agreed. I've attached the high-res logo set in case you need different sizes (Acuvera_Logo_SVG.zip). Once you update the Order Form with the 4-day approval window and the 7-day post-signature embargo clause, please re-send via DocuSign and we'll return signatures quickly.

Appreciate it — Susan
